provenance: I authored the Unique formalization and its additional evaluation checks, but did not author Shared or the correspondence implementation. For this cross-layer review I read all required authored units, exact Lean selections and the review-policy snapshot; I also inspected the named definitions and statement assumptions in any additionally listed source context. I compared the Shared design independently, found and requested correction of a stored-mode/path-mode wording mismatch, then reread the changed shared.steps snapshot and verified other required inputs unchanged before deciding. Listing a containing source context records the inspected definitions, not an audit of every proof tactic in that file.
rationale: unit:shared.steps introduces configuration and ordered statement sequence P; shared.state/shared.syntax/shared.resolution/shared.give supply storage, expression, path and permission meanings. Configuration.initial and finished match empty storage plus full code and completion at empty code. Eval.give and Eval.giveShare delegate to Give, with giveShare changing only the returned mode. Eval.new requires class membership, EvalArgs, matching field/result lengths and absence of the post-argument counter identity; State.allocate installs those results in field order and returns a unique new reference. EvalArgs.cons threads the first result state into the rest, so nesting and allocation occur left to right inside a single Step.letValue. The latter checks absence in the evaluated variable table and binds only after complete evaluation. The inspected WellFormedWith and Eval.preserves_wellFormedWith statements account for pending results as additional owners until construction/binding. The corrected repeated-give sentence now distinguishes effective path access from the final stored mode: shared access may promote and then copy, while entirely unique access clears the slot. Steps and Stuck match finite successful transitions and unfinished configurations without any successor; no partial failed state is exposed.
limitations: This comparison checks prose/notation and formal statement correspondence; it does not independently certify Lean proof checking or audit proof tactics.
Lean uses raw lists for tables; finite-map reading and single-slot identity rely on the explicitly separate key-distinctness/well-formedness conditions.
